headline: Opposed Statewide Ballot Question 8; ordered Amazon drone delivery community forum; referred blighted-property fines ordinance to committee.
summary: Members voted 6-0, with five abstentions, to oppose Statewide Ballot Question 8. They adopted an order for a community forum on Amazon's expected Prime Air drone service after an earlier vote failed. They referred a draft ordinance on escalating fines for blighted properties to committee, and sent many traffic, sidewalk, and street petitions to committees.
decisions: Adopted resolution opposing Statewide Ballot Question 8 and urging a no vote on November 3, 2026, 6 yeas, 0 nays, 5 abstentions.
Adopted order asking the Mayor to consider an informational statement on the pros and cons of Question 8.
Adopted as amended order asking the City Manager to identify funding for toilet seats in new Institute Park bathrooms and report on best practices.
Referred sidewalk, streetlight, and sidewalk-repair petitions on Beeching St., Coburn Ave., and Shrewsbury St. to Public Works Committee.
Referred request to trim city tree at 42 Agate Ave. to the Department of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery.
Referred 17 traffic, speed, and parking petitions (items 7e through 7u) to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Set November 10, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. hearings on conduit locations at 135 Kenberma Rd., Main St., and Newbury St.
Referred request to review the Union Station pickup and drop-off area to the City Manager.
Adopted five committee orders on signs, survey markers, spray parks, European Starlings, and the Salisbury Pond Dam.
Adopted order asking the Parks Commissioner to review and repair the basketball court driveway on Coburn Ave.
Referred order on street and sidewalk resurfacing review to Public Works Committee.
Adopted order asking the Public Works Commissioner and Chief Financial Officer to speed up bidding for street and sidewalk resurfacing.
Motion to place the blighted-property fines item on file was denied, 2 yeas and 9 nays.
Referred blighted-property escalating fines ordinance item to Economic Development Committee as amended, 9 yeas and 2 nays.
Adopted order asking the Police Chief for increased speed and traffic enforcement on Goddard Memorial Dr. near Beatrice Dr.
Placed on file order to require tree planting by contractors in curb and sidewalk contracts.
Order denied on Amazon drone community forum related zoning report request, 5 yeas and 6 nays.
Adopted order requesting a community forum on Amazon's expected Prime Air drone service, 10 yeas and 1 nay.
Reconsideration of the Amazon drone forum order was denied, 0 yeas and 11 nays.
Adopted order asking Public Works for a report on a proactive annual pothole repair program and sidewalk review.
Adopted as amended order for a citywide survey and replacement of damaged or illegible street and traffic signs.
Adopted resolution affirming support for workers' rights, 11 yeas and 0 nays.
Accepted and adopted honorary street name for Oread St. and five resurfacing committee orders.
Accepted committee recommendation to give the petitioner leave to withdraw the sidewalk resurfacing request from 31 Mower St. to 67 Mower St.
Accepted committee recommendation to give the petitioner leave to withdraw the Puritan Ave. street resurfacing request.
Referred crosswalk curb cut request at Laurel St. and Everett Gaylord Blvd. to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Accepted and adopted order extending city spray park hours by one hour, one day a week, for the 2027 season.
Accepted parks committee reports, including two petitions recommended to be placed on file.
Placed on file communication on how the U.S. Department of Justice report on Worcester Police differs from the city's account, 8 yeas and 2 nays.
Motion to table the U.S. Department of Justice report item was denied, 2 yeas and 8 nays.
Adopted order asking the Commissioners to notify students about pedestrian safety measures near schools, 11 yeas and 0 nays.
Adopted order requesting a copy of the two-year Safe Routes to School Taskforce strategic plan, 11 yeas and 0 nays.
Adopted order asking the Transportation Commissioner to consider hybrid beacons at Chandler Elementary crosswalks, 11 yeas and 0 nays.
Adopted order requesting a report on parking rules near Roosevelt and Rice Square elementary schools, 11 yeas and 0 nays.
Referred review of Rule Five on special meetings of City Council to Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 8 yeas and 3 nays.
Adopted order requesting a report on why pedestrian hybrid beacons were ruled out at Fremont, Canterbury, and Cambridge streets.
Adopted order asking for example ordinances on escalating fines for blighted properties from similarly populated cities.
Adopted order requesting a report on federal and state rules for drone launch sites on publicly-owned land.
